newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt paper prices seen rising at trading.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt paper prices seen rising at trading.

text.p: The unplaced remainder of bids from Wednesday's auctions of GKO discount Treasury bills and OFZ interest-bearing bonds of 2.5 trillion roubles will help a price rise of 0.2-0.4 percentage points at today's trading session, dealers said.
There will be a one hour trading session after the auctions ahead of the May 1-4 holidays. There is usually no trading on Wednesdays.

"The auctions were up to dealers' expectations," said Naztionalny Rezervny Bank dealer Stanislav Litvinov. "We even got a tiny premium for the T-bill issue. But those who wanted to buy have already bought, that's why we do not expect a significant price rise. There is nowhere to push the price."
The annualised average yield on an issue of 322-day T-bill was 30.64 percent and the average price of a 728-day bond was 98.26 percent.
